note: Editorial milestones pinned to original captured events. Missing evidence is omitted; timestamps always come from source events.

chapters.title: FLUJO joins the conversation
chapters.description: The first team-channel ping reaches FLUJO, and its response is persisted in the local conversation history.

chapters.title: Codex takes the supervisor role
chapters.description: A dedicated supervisor reviews pull requests while parallel sessions own frontend, backend, dataset and MCP work.

chapters.title: Development splits into workstreams
chapters.description: The team reports five parallel sessions: frontend, backend, dataset, MCP, and supervision/review.

chapters.title: A FLUJO team governs the release loop
chapters.description: Codex sets up a FLUJO release team with a supervisor, builder, product auditor, independent reviewer and watchdog. A recurring coordinator keeps the work moving.

chapters.title: Local and Modal CI become recurring
chapters.description: The team chooses hourly Windows/Docker verification and a daily Modal run. The saved automation and a later completed local run provide distinct configuration and execution evidence.
